chunks: Muhammad b. Ibrahim b. Ishaq (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad al-Hamadani informed us. He said: Ali b. al-Hasan b. Ali b. Faddal informed us from his father from Abu al-Hasan Ali b. Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him), that he said:
We are masters in this world and kings in the Hereafter.

key_terms.سادة: Masters, lords, leaders (plural of sayyid) — referring to the Imams as spiritual and religious guides
key_terms.ملوك: Kings, sovereigns (plural of malik) — their royal and exalted status in the Hereafter

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Rida say about the status of the Ahlulbayt in this world and the Hereafter?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him), the eighth Shia Imam, declares the elevated, divinely-ordained status of the Ahlulbayt — the Prophet's household — as masters (sada) in the temporal world and kings (muluk) in the eternal Hereafter. This tradition, narrated through a chain reaching back to a major Fathite transmitter, was recorded by Sheikh Saduq in his Amali assemblies and affirms the Shia creedal position on Imamate and the supreme authority of the Imams. The audience of early Shia listeners would have understood 'masters' to refer to spiritual and religious leadership, and 'kings' to indicate the exalted eschatological reward reserved for the Imams.
